identity._note: platform from the 17-entry platform_to_cstr enum; device count from multi_device_info_count

public_endpoints._note: server-reflexive candidate from call signalling — full address and port, not masked

private_endpoints._note: host candidate from the peer's own LAN or carrier NAT; delivered even when the two sides are on different networks

telemetry_view._note: the telemetry path masks the peer address to /24 while the signalling path above does not

medium.peer_meaning: not cellular (Wi-Fi, or Ethernet on a desktop peer)
medium.self_meaning: not cellular (Wi-Fi, or Ethernet on a desktop peer)

nat._note: p2p_disabled is the desktop equivalent of Android's disallowAllP2P(). False means 'Protect IP address in calls' was not in effect. Media going over a relay does not imply the address was protected — candidates are still exchanged either way.

latency._note: peer is farther from this relay than we are
peer is closer to this relay than we are

relays._note: identical or negative peer values are placeholders; no location inference can be drawn from them. A mixed profile (closer to some relays, farther from others) is more discriminating than a uniform one.

speech_activity._note: speech energy sampled by the client; zeros are silence

behaviour._note: dtx_rx_duration_t is how long the peer transmitted nothing

fingerprint._note: rx-side values describe what the peer produced

correlation._note: the bucket id was identical across three calls to the same device, so it links calls over a short window. It tracks the DEVICE: another device on the same account gave a different platform, version and LAN address.

self._note: included so peer values can be told apart from ours

caveats: No JID or phone number exists on this layer — confirmed across three runs; the VoIP layer works with a call id instead.
No location data in call signalling; relay latency is the only geographic proxy and it is not always a real measurement.
battery_low is present in telemetry but which side it belongs to was never established.
WAM hooks did not fire during calls, so the messaging surface is not covered here.
